context: The five-level pyramid widens from top to bottom. The top three levels sit inside a green box labeled CPU and are grouped under “Cache” on the left. The fourth level is labeled “Main memory” and the fifth “Disk.”

frames.explanation: An upward arrow on the right reads “Speed, price”: higher levels provide faster access at a higher cost per unit of storage. A downward arrow reads “Capacity, persistence”: capacity increases toward the bottom, where HDDs and SSDs can retain data long after power is removed. Cache and main memory are volatile and lose their data when power is removed.
frames.title: Levels of the computer memory and storage hierarchy

summary: The pyramid compares speed, capacity, cost per unit of storage, and persistence across levels.
